fact: The article calls the Cybercrime Act of 2025 Liberia's recently enacted law and reports police charging a suspect under it on 21-22 September 2026.

Police detained commentator Jerry Nyantee Wrato from 17 September 2026 over AI-generated images of the Vice President and, per the Inspector General's 21 September letter, resolved to prosecute him under Sections 10.1, 15.1, 18.1 and 19.1 of the Act (misuse of devices, cyberstalking, incitement, harmful data messages); a court ordered him released on habeas corpus on 22 September.
The article says the Cybercrime Act of 2025 was passed by the Senate in November 2025 and signed into law, quoting an official that President Boakai signed it on 19 August 2026.
Jerry Nyantee Wrotto was arrested for allegedly creating and posting AI-generated nude images and video of Vice President Koung, the arrest being presented as the Act's first major public test.
The article says President Boakai signed the Cybercrime Act into law on 19 August 2026 and that the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications has published the approved Act.

Police arrested Jerry Nyantee Wrotto over the weekend before 21 September 2026 over AI-generated images of Vice President Koung, and the Inspector General confirmed the arrest was made under the Cybercrime Law; no court had yet ruled on the conduct.

The article says the Cybercrime Act of 2025 is now formally published as an approved Act, listed by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications and published by the Executive Mansion, and that Liberia has entered the enforcement phase.
President Boakai signed the Cybercrime Act into law, announced on 19 August 2026, per the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.

Senator Moye said on 30 June 2026 that a comprehensive cybersecurity bill passed by both Houses awaited only President Boakai's signature to become law (article published 2026-07-01; event date taken from the publication date).
The Senate notified the House of its concurrence in passing the Cybercrime Act of 2025, clearing the bill for presidential signature, which was still awaited.

Police announced four charges under the Cybercrime Act against Jerry Nyantee Wrato, arrested over allegedly manipulated digital content involving Vice President Koung; he was later released from custody after court intervention (arrest date not given; article published 2026-09-24 used).
President Boakai signed the Cybercrime Act and Data Protection Act into law, publicly announced on 19 August 2026 by Posts and Telecommunications Minister Kromah.

The article states President Boakai approved the Cybercrime Act on 3 July 2026, after House passage on 28 September 2023 and Senate passage on 20 November 2025; it notes that the Act requires regulations within six to twelve months.

The New Republic reports that Liberia's Cybersecurity and Cybercrime Act was passed by the Legislature and is being operationalized by the Liberia Telecommunications Authority and the Ministry of Justice (no earlier date given, so the 2026-09-24 publication date is used).

The Liberia National Police arrested a citizen, Jerry Nyanti Wratto, for posts about Vice President Koung, held him at police headquarters, and charged him and forwarded him to court on four alleged offences citing sections 10.1, 15.1, 18.1 and 19.1 of the Cybercrime Act; the article gives the arrest as 'this week' of 2026-09-24.

The Analyst reports that Liberia's Cybercrime Act, which Senator Konneh voted for, was recently passed and is the subject of first enforcement actions (no passage date given, so the 2026-09-24 publication date is used).

The Analyst reports the arrest of Jerry Nyantee Wrato over AI-generated images and videos of Vice President Koung, and says the Liberia National Police will forward him to court on four counts under the Cybercrime Act of 2025; the charges are untested in court (arrest date not given, 2026-09-24 publication date used).

The Liberian Observer reports that ten civil society organisations plan to engage lawmakers on amendments to Liberia's Cybercrime Act of 2025, treating it as an existing law (no enactment date given, so the 2026-09-24 publication date is used).

President Boakai approved Liberia's Cybercrime Act on 3 July 2026 after the House (28 September 2023) and Senate (20 November 2025) passed it, and the Executive was enforcing it by October 2026, according to The Liberian Investigator.

The Liberian Investigator reports the arrest, days before 15 October 2026, of Jerry Nyantee Wrotto, accused of cyberbullying the Vice President with AI-generated images and videos, as Senator Dopoh said the Executive was enforcing the Act prematurely.
The Liberian Senate passed the Cybercrime Act of 2025 'a few days' before 11 November 2025, according to a Liberian Observer opinion piece; the piece does not say it is in force.
The Liberian Senate passed the Cybercrime Act of 2025, described as a proposed Act, with amendments on 4 November 2025, after a joint committee report; the document does not say it was promulgated.
Post and Telecommunications Minister Kromah announced that President Boakai has signed the Cybercrime Act into law; the Senate had passed the 2025 act with amendments on 4 November 2025.
Senator Cyrus cited Liberia's Cybercrime Act of 2025 as an important step in its legal framework, warning that legislation alone will not secure the country without funding and capable institutions.
